speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me assess your hematuria and right flank pain, can you tell me if you have experienced any fever, chills, or nausea? Additionally, does the pain radiate toward your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Do you have any history of kidney stones, and does the pain come in waves or stay constant? I will also request a urinalysis and a non-contrast CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis to look for stones or other causes.
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis
REQUEST TEST: CT_Abdomen_Pelvis_Non_Contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT scan is normal, which makes kidney stones unlikely despite the flank pain and hematuria. Given the positive leukocyte esterase and significant white blood cells in the urine, this points toward an infection like pyelonephritis rather than a stone. Do you have any fever or chills, and does the pain feel constant rather than colicky?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned a history of recurrent UTIs, which is significant given the negative CT scan. Since the imaging ruled out stones, I need to know if you are currently experiencing fever, chills, or nausea to confirm if this is an active kidney infection like pyelonephritis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: You haven't confirmed whether you have a fever, chills, or nausea, which are critical for diagnosing pyelonephritis. Please clarify if you are experiencing any of these systemic symptoms right now.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal and you lack systemic symptoms like fever, kidney infection is unlikely. I need to check for other causes of hematuria, so do you have any history of high blood pressure or protein in your urine? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Protein_Creatinine_Ratio

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and no signs of infection or proteinuria, I need to rule out malignancy or structural issues. Do you have any history of smoking, or have you noticed any palpable masses in your abdomen? REQUEST TEST: Urine_Cytology

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative cytology and normal imaging make malignancy unlikely. Given the recurrent UTIs, hematuria, and flank pain without stones or infection signs, I suspect Interstitial Cystitis or a similar inflammatory condition. DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis
